Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

king noun

also monarch, sovereign

classical

Cic. Rep. 1.42
Tac. Ann. 1.1
Traupman 51–52

rēx, rēgis m.

noun, third declension

Cicero’s definition: when the whole state is in one man’s hands, rēgem illum ūnum vocāmus (Rep. 1.42). After the last Tarquin was driven out the Romans hated the name; the word serves for the kings of every age and people. Also the king in chess and in cards (Traupman 51–52).

Examples

  • Urbem Rōmam ā prīncipiō rēgēs habuēre

    At first the city of Rome was ruled by kingsTac. Ann. 1.1

  • quī fuit rāna, nunc est rēx

    the one who was a frog is now a kingPetr. 77.1

See also queen, prince, princess, emperor, palace, castle, rule.
